claims.statement: proxy.ts is non-gating by design: its clerkMiddleware handler only stamps `x-pathname` from the request URL onto the forwarded headers and calls NextResponse.next(), performing no session check and no redirect, so authentication must be enforced by the component that renders protected data.

proxy.ts's matcher names `/(api|trpc)(.*)`, so the middleware runs on API routes and Clerk's inbound webhook reaches the app through it rather than being short-circuited; that webhook is unauthenticated because the handler verifies Clerk's signature with verifyWebhook against CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET.
The x-pathname header is presentation-only and is the only thing the middleware produces: the layout derives `isTrainerRoute` from it and the sign-in layout reads it, but nothing authorizes on it.

Both x-pathname consumers default a missing header to the empty string, which silently reads as 'office route': `isTrainerRoute` stays false and the trainer-only nav omissions lapse while a client island resolves the real path from usePathname(), so the two views can disagree.

app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx is the sole authentication gate: its first statement is requireAuthenticatedUser(), which redirects to /sign-in when the Clerk session has no userId, and the Playwright spec asserts exactly that redirect rather than anything in proxy.ts.

A route outside the (dashboard) group is unguarded until it adds its own check: app/api-docs calls requireAuthenticatedUser itself, while app/sign-in, app/sign-up and the machine-reached app/api/* rely on having none.

A failed profile read does not abort the dashboard layout: role resolves null and tenants to [], the shell renders a smaller menu, and the page renders beneath it, so the nav hides the admin and platform rows rather than denying them and each route must re-check its own authority.
Office screens take the school from the URL path segment, and app/(dashboard)/t/[tenantCode]/layout.tsx turns that into a validated scope before any page in the segment renders.

resolveRouteScope returns a four-way union and the segment layout renders each arm distinctly: `ok` passes children through, `no-tenant-access` renders NoTenantAccessState, `unknown` renders a try-again state, and `not-a-member` renders 'School not available' with a link to the caller's fallback school when one exists.

A TenantScope is selection, not authorization: scopeForCode builds one only for a code in the caller's own profile.tenants (lowercased on both sides), so an unknown or foreign code yields null and the query filter only picks among schools RLS already allows.

requireScope returns null instead of calling notFound() because a layout and its page render in parallel, so a thrown 404 could race the layout's friendlier state; with no scope there is no tenant id to query with, so security does not rest on the choice.

The segment layout is the only place that renders a scope state; pages call requireScope() and `return null` on a non-ok result, and a page that forgets that guard falls through to running with an undefined tenant id.

The legacy unscoped paths are one-line stubs from the legacyRoute() factory: redirectToDefaultScope re-encodes the caller's search params onto /t/<default school>/<section> and redirects, rendering only when there is no school to send the caller to, and /dashboard puts the trusted-role dispatch (trainer to /trainer, admin to /overview) in front of it.
Trainer routes are deliberately unscoped because a batch carries its tenant (ADR-001 K1-redirect), and the private SCOPED_SECTIONS list is what keeps them outside the scoped tree.

The shell decides its trainer variant from x-pathname rather than the caller's role: Sidebar.resolveOperations keeps only the Settings op and drops the admin/platform lists on a trainer route, and Topbar hides the per-school activity bell there.

resolveTrustedRole is the only role source allowed to decide a redirect or an authorization: it reads profiles.role alone, never Clerk metadata, and returns null rather than a default when there is no profile row.

billing and report refuse a trainer with redirect('/trainer') gated on resolveTrustedRole alone, because resolveRouteRole's ?role= preview would let a real trainer request ?role=admin and skip the gate.

Trainer refusal also relies on the dashboard layout's single trusted read: the t/[school]/dashboard page redirects on profile.role straight off the already-validated scope instead of taking a second profile read.

Presentation uses toOfficeRole/resolveDisplayRole, which collapse anything that is not an office role — trainer, null, an unknown string — to the least-privileged read-only viewer, pinned by unit tests that call the pair a usability gate with RLS as the real boundary.
The least-privilege viewer fallback is load-bearing in both directions: a viewer is denied writes by RLS rather than by hidden buttons, because can_manage_tenant admits only admin and coordinator.
/dashboard is a router, not a screen: it sends trainers to /trainer, admins to /overview and everyone else to their default school's dashboard, all on the trusted profile.role read.
/overview is the one unscoped office screen, admits admins only via resolveTrustedRole and redirects everyone else to /dashboard, and returns a NoTenantAccessState when the caller has no memberships.

Tenant access and route scope answer orthogonal questions: resolveTenantAccess asks whether the caller belongs to any school, and the unknown verdict is never rendered as none because a 'could not check' failure would tell a provisioned coordinator they were never assigned.

getSignedInProfile and resolveRouteScope are cache()-wrapped so a layout and its page share one profile read per request, and a failed identity read collapses to 'unknown' while a missing profile row collapses to 'none', never the reverse.

app/(dashboard)/t/loading.tsx sits above [tenantCode]/layout.tsx on purpose, because a loading file does not cover its own folder's layout and that layout awaits the school scope; placing it inside the segment would leave a school switch blank.

app/ is the only layer allowed to compose these reads, so the route-tree joins of auth identity and tenancy profile live there (tenant-access.ts, tenant-scope.ts) because a module may not import another module's private data/ layer.

GET /api/openapi.json performs its own getAuthUserId() check and answers 401 without a session; POST /api/webhooks/clerk has no session check because Clerk signs the body and verifyWebhook rejects a bad signature with 400; GET /api/health is unauthenticated on purpose for probes; GET /api/debug/auth-check is deliberately dev-only (404 in production) because it returns the raw Supabase and token detail RULES rule 6 keeps out of the UI. A new /api route gets no upstream gate, so it must carry its own.

requireAuthenticatedUser() returns a string and never a nullable: callers get the Clerk id or the /sign-in redirect, so a page cannot continue with null. app/api-docs/page.tsx is the page outside the (dashboard) group that calls it itself.

The (dashboard) layout derives every nav input from trusted sources — resolveTrustedRole plus one getProfileSnapshot()/isPlatformAdmin() Promise.all — never resolveRouteRole, whose ?role= preview would let any caller conjure the admin-only row; isPlatformAdmin is a separate axis read from platform_admins via a security definer RPC because that table is unreadable through the anon client.

The (dashboard) layout renders no KPI row because a root layout does not re-render on client-side navigation, so a row there kept the previous school's numbers after a school switch; only the two dashboard pages render one.

requireScope redirects a trainer to /trainer once the scope resolves ok, before any page fetches, because these screens hand full batch DTOs to client components, which RULES rule 5 forbids; the check lives in the page path rather than the layout because a layout does not re-run on every navigation. The segment layout renders every non-ok arm because it is the only component in the segment guaranteed to run and to own a state instead of data.

Two routes outside the (dashboard) group are deliberately public and each authenticates its own caller: /sign-in and /sign-up must stay open or sign-in could not be reached. /sign-in composes the attacker-controlled redirect_url through sanitizeRedirectUrl, a pure function returning "/" unless the value is a genuine same-origin path; the traps it closes (absolute scheme, //evil.com, /\evil.com, javascript:/data:) are all browser misresolutions, and tests/unit/redirect-url.test.ts pins each one.

redirectToDefaultScope re-appends every incoming search param value into URLSearchParams before redirecting back under /t/<default school>/<section>, so a deep link keeps its batch parameter; a stub that redirected with a bare path would instead drop the caller onto the section's default view.

/t/loading.tsx sits above the [tenantCode] layout on purpose: a loading file does not cover its own folder's layout and that layout awaits the school scope, so this skeleton is what shows during a school switch.

tests/unit/session-exists.test.ts pins isSessionExistsError matching a session_exists code anywhere in errors[] and ignoring other codes and non-array throwals, the forwarding case the sign-in screen depends on.
